answer: Think of identity issuance as a prism: one funding source entering it should come out as a single beam, not a spray of clones. A registry charges each new identity a fee that rises steeply with how many identities its wallet or hardware fingerprint already holds — the first costs a walnut, the hundredth costs a fortune. A comet of fresh Sybils therefore burns its whole budget on the first few copies, while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
